2. Neither Nadia nor Khalid is selected.
3. If Owais is selected, then Uzma is not selected.
4. Javeria is selected.

pz-x004.x:
Six swimmers — Nadia, Junaid, Yasir, Sadia, Umair and Kamran — compete in a final at a district meet, with no ties.

Rules:
1. Nadia and Kamran do not finish in consecutive positions.
2. Yasir and Kamran finish in consecutive positions.
3. Sadia and Umair do not finish in consecutive positions.
4. Sadia does not finish first or last.
5. At least one of the following is true: Sadia finishes in position 4; Sadia finishes immediately ahead of Nadia.

pz-x005.x:
Seven passengers — Zubair, Wardah, Raheel, Qasim, Tahira, Mahnoor and Babar — stand in a single queue at a railway ticket window, in positions 1 (front) to 7 (back).

Rules:
1. Zubair and Babar stand next to each other in the queue.
2. If Qasim stands ahead of Babar, then Babar stands at the front or at the back of the queue.
3. At least one of the following is true: Wardah and Qasim stand next to each other in the queue; Wardah stands ahead of Babar.
4. Tahira stands ahead of Wardah.
5. Mahnoor stands immediately ahead of Babar.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the order of speakers, from first to sixth?
o: Ayesha, Bilal, Farah, Danish, Hamza, Imran
Ayesha, Imran, Hamza, Farah, Danish, Bilal
Ayesha, Bilal, Danish, Hamza, Imran, Farah
Bilal, Ayesha, Hamza, Imran, Farah, Danish
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Ayesha, Imran, Hamza, Farah, Danish, Bilal satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Bilal speaks before Ayesha; Danish does not follow Farah immediately; Farah speaks before Imran.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Imran must speak before Farah, so Farah cannot be first. The other three can happen: Ayesha, Imran, Hamza, Bilal, Farah, Danish has Danish sixth; Ayesha, Bilal, Hamza, Imran, Farah, Danish has Bilal second; Ayesha, Imran, Farah, Danish, Hamza, Bilal has Hamza fifth.

questions.s: If Hamza speaks second, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Imran and Farah both speak before Danish, so at least two speakers precede him. With Hamza second, those two cannot be first and second together, so Danish is at least fourth and certainly after Hamza. The others fail in valid orders such as Ayesha, Hamza, Imran, Bilal, Farah, Danish, where Bilal comes after Imran and Farah is fifth, and Imran, Hamza, Ayesha, Bilal, Farah, Danish, where Ayesha is not first.

questions.s: If Bilal speaks before Imran, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Ayesha, Bilal, Imran and Farah are now in a fixed order, and Danish follows Farah directly. Hamza cannot be first or last, so he goes into places two to four, never between Farah and Danish. Farah is therefore always fifth and Danish sixth. Hamza may be second, third or fourth, so the other options are not forced.

questions.s: If Farah speaks second, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Farah second forces Imran first and Danish third. Ayesha, Hamza and Bilal then fill places four to six with Ayesha before Bilal and Hamza not last, so Hamza must be fourth or fifth. Hamza fourth works (Ayesha fifth, Bilal sixth). Bilal fifth would leave Hamza sixth, Ayesha third is taken by Danish, and Hamza sixth is not allowed.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the seating, from chair 1 to chair 6?
o: Kiran, Nadia, Omar, Saad, Tariq, Rabia
Kiran, Saad, Nadia, Omar, Rabia, Tariq
Tariq, Saad, Omar, Kiran, Nadia, Rabia
Kiran, Nadia, Omar, Rabia, Saad, Tariq
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Tariq, Saad, Omar, Kiran, Nadia, Rabia satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Kiran and Nadia are not neighbours; Tariq sits in a middle chair; Rabia and Saad are neighbours.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Omar sits to the left of Rabia, so Omar cannot take chair 6, the last place on the right. Rabia in chair 2 (Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq), Kiran in chair 6 (Tariq, Saad, Omar, Rabia, Nadia, Kiran) and Saad in chair 5 (the same order as the first) all occur in valid seatings.

questions.s: If Tariq sits in chair 6, which one of the following must be true?
o: Saad does not sit in chair 4
questions.e: With Tariq in chair 6, Saad must be in chair 2, 3 or 5. Suppose Saad is in chair 4: chairs 1, 2, 3 and 5 are left for Kiran, Nadia, Omar and Rabia. Kiran and Nadia must be neighbours, so they take 1 and 2 or 2 and 3. Rabia cannot be in chair 3 or 5 (next to Saad) and must be right of Omar, so Omar is 1 and Rabia 2, which leaves Kiran and Nadia in chairs 3 and 5, not neighbours. So Saad is never in chair 4. Each other option fails in a valid seating, for example Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq.

questions.s: If Kiran sits in chair 3, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Kiran in chair 3 puts Nadia in chair 2 or 4. Nadia in chair 5 is impossible because it is not next to chair 3, Saad in chair 6 and Tariq in chair 4 break the rules about ends, while Rabia in chair 2 works in Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq.

questions.s: If Omar sits in chair 1, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Tariq must sit at an end. With Omar in chair 1, that end is taken, so Tariq is in chair 6. The other options are possible but not forced: Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq has Saad in chair 5 and Rabia in chair 2; Omar, Saad, Kiran, Nadia, Rabia, Tariq has Rabia in chair 5; Omar, Rabia, Nadia, Kiran, Saad, Tariq has Nadia in chair 3.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the order of sessions from Monday to Saturday?
o: Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art
Debate, Quiz, Chess, Art, Drama, Calligraphy
Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Drama
Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Art, Drama, Chess
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Chess is not on the day before Art; Drama is on Monday or Saturday; Calligraphy is not two days after Debate.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Calligraphy is held two days after Debate, so it cannot be earlier than Wednesday. Drama on Tuesday works in Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Quiz, Chess, Art; Quiz on Saturday works in Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Quiz; Art on Tuesday works in Chess, Art, Drama, Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy.

questions.s: If Drama is held on Tuesday, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Debate cannot be on Tuesday, which is Drama's day. Debate on Wednesday or Thursday would put Calligraphy on Friday or Saturday and leave no two consecutive free days for Chess and Art. So Debate is on Monday and Calligraphy on Wednesday. The other options fail in Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Quiz.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Drama on Thursday works in Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art. Quiz cannot be on Monday because Debate comes first. Debate on Tuesday would put Calligraphy on Thursday, and the only consecutive free days for Chess and Art would be Friday and Saturday, which forces Drama onto Monday. Art on Wednesday would put Chess on Tuesday and force Drama onto Monday as well.

questions.s: On how many different days of the week could the Drama session be held?
questions.e: Only five orders satisfy the rules: Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art (Drama on Thursday); Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Quiz, Chess, Art and Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Quiz (Tuesday); Chess, Art, Drama, Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy (Wednesday); Chess, Art, Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Quiz (Thursday). So Drama can fall on Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, three days.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the Red team?
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Uzma, Faisal, Hina, Junaid satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Faisal and Hina are in different teams; Junaid and Maryam are in the same team; Sana is in Faisal's team.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
o: Junaid is in the Red team
Zainab is in the Blue team
Sana and Hina are in different teams
Naveed is in the Blue team
questions.e: Hina is always in Faisal's team, and Sana is never in Faisal's team, so Sana and Hina are never together. The other options fail in valid divisions: Naveed is Red in Uzma, Junaid, Naveed, Sana; Zainab is Red in Uzma, Zainab, Junaid, Sana; Junaid is Blue in Uzma, Zainab, Maryam, Sana.

questions.s: If Zainab is in the Red team, which one of the following must be true?
o: Junaid is in the Red team
Faisal is in the Blue team
Maryam is in the Blue team
Naveed is in the Red team
questions.e: Red already holds Uzma, Zainab and one of Junaid and Maryam, who must be split, so only one place is left. Faisal and Hina need two places together, so they are both Blue. Sana cannot be with Faisal, so she joins Red. The Red team is then Uzma, Zainab, Sana and either Junaid or Maryam, so neither of those two is forced, while Naveed is always Blue.

questions.s: If Junaid is in the Blue team, which one of the following could be true?
o: Hina and Zainab are both in the Red team
Maryam is in the Blue team
Naveed is in the Red team
Zainab and Naveed are both in the Red team
questions.e: Junaid in Blue puts Maryam in Red. Red: Uzma, Maryam, Naveed, Sana with Blue: Zainab, Faisal, Hina, Junaid satisfies every rule, so Naveed can be Red. Maryam cannot be Blue. Zainab and Naveed both in Red with Uzma and Maryam would leave Sana in Blue with Faisal and Hina. Hina and Zainab both in Red would bring Faisal too, so Red would be full without Maryam.

questions.s: If Sana and Zainab are in different teams, which one of the following must be true?
o: Naveed is in the Red team
Maryam is in the Red team
Junaid is in the Blue team
Faisal and Hina are in the Red team
questions.e: Suppose Zainab were Red and Sana Blue. Faisal would then be Red, with Hina, making Red Uzma, Zainab, Faisal, Hina and putting Junaid and Maryam together in Blue, which is not allowed. So Zainab is Blue and Sana is Red. Faisal and Hina then go Blue, away from Sana, and Red needs two more: one of Junaid and Maryam, and Naveed.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the committee?
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Usman, Waqar, Yasir, Mehwish satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Usman and Zara are both chosen; neither Asad nor Mehwish is chosen; Shahid is chosen without Waqar.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Suppose Waqar were left out. Yasir would be out as well, and Shahid could not be chosen, so the four members would have to come from Usman, Zara, Asad and Mehwish. That would include both Usman and Zara, which is not allowed. So Waqar, and with him Yasir, is always chosen. The other options each fail in some valid committee, for example Asad, Waqar, Yasir, Zara has no Usman, and Mehwish, Waqar, Yasir, Zara has no Asad.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
o: Zara and Shahid are both chosen
Usman and Mehwish are both chosen
Shahid and Asad are both chosen
Zara and Mehwish are both chosen
questions.e: Zara and Shahid together need Waqar and Yasir as well, which fills all four places and leaves neither Asad nor Mehwish. Each of the other pairs fits a valid committee: Mehwish, Usman, Waqar, Yasir; Asad, Shahid, Waqar, Yasir; Mehwish, Waqar, Yasir, Zara.

questions.s: If Usman is chosen, which one of the following must be true?
o: Asad and Mehwish are both chosen
questions.e: Usman is chosen, so Zara is out. Waqar and Yasir are always chosen, which makes three members, and the fourth must be Asad or Mehwish, so Shahid is left out. Asad is not forced, since Mehwish can be chosen instead, and both together would make five.

questions.s: If Mehwish is not chosen, which one of the following could be true?
o: Shahid and Usman are both chosen
questions.e: Without Mehwish, Asad is needed. With Waqar and Yasir also chosen, one place remains, and Zara can fill it (Asad, Waqar, Yasir, Zara). Asad cannot be left out, Waqar cannot be left out, and Shahid with Usman would make five members.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the seating, from chair 1 to chair 6?
o: Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Yousaf, Zubair
Saima, Usama, Zubair, Talha, Wajiha, Yousaf
Yousaf, Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair
Saima, Talha, Zubair, Usama, Wajiha, Yousaf
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Yousaf, Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Saima and Talha are not opposite each other; Usama and Wajiha are not neighbours; Yousaf sits next to Talha and Zubair is not next to Talha.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Put Saima in chair 1 and Talha opposite in chair 4; turning the table does not change the argument. Zubair must be next to Talha, in chair 3 or 5. Yousaf cannot be next to Talha either, so he cannot take the other of those chairs, and the only chairs left for him are 2 and 6, both next to Saima. The other options fail in Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair, Yousaf: Usama is not next to Talha, Wajiha is not next to Saima, and Usama is not opposite Zubair.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Zubair sits next to Talha, and Talha is opposite Saima, so Zubair is two places away from Saima, never beside her. Usama next to Saima, Wajiha next to Talha and Wajiha opposite Zubair all occur, for example in Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair, Yousaf.

questions.s: If Usama sits in chair 4, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Usama in chair 4 puts Wajiha in chair 3 or 5. Talha, Zubair, Yousaf and Saima must fill the four other chairs in a row, in that order or the reverse, so Wajiha in chair 5 works in Zubair, Yousaf, Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha. Wajiha cannot be in chair 2, which is not next to Usama. Talha in chair 1 would put Saima opposite in chair 4, where Usama sits, and Yousaf in chair 5 would need both Saima and Zubair in chairs 4 and 6.

questions.s: If Usama sits next to Talha, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Talha's neighbours are now Zubair and Usama. Usama's other neighbour is Wajiha, and Saima, opposite Talha, completes the circle between Wajiha and Yousaf, so the order round the table is Wajiha, Usama, Talha, Zubair, Yousaf, Saima. Wajiha is therefore next to Saima. Usama is not next to Saima or Yousaf, and Wajiha is not next to Talha.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the timetable, with the morning paper named first each day?
o: Mon Maths, English; Tue Urdu, Physics; Wed Chemistry, Biology
Mon Urdu, Physics; Tue Chemistry, Biology; Wed English, Maths
Mon Maths, Urdu; Tue English, Physics; Wed Chemistry, Biology
Mon English, Maths; Tue Physics, Urdu; Wed Chemistry, Biology
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Mon Maths, Urdu; Tue English, Physics; Wed Chemistry, Biology satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Maths is not on an earlier day than Physics; English is in an evening session; Physics is in a morning session.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
o: Urdu is held in a morning session
Maths is not held on Wednesday
questions.e: Physics must be on a later day than Maths, so Physics cannot be on Monday, and Maths must be on Monday or Tuesday. Hence Maths is never on Wednesday, the option that must hold. Chemistry on Wednesday, Urdu in the morning and Physics on Tuesday each occur in some valid timetables but not in all.

questions.s: If Chemistry is held on Tuesday, which one of the following must be true?
o: Maths is held in a morning session
Biology is held in a morning session
questions.e: Chemistry and Biology fill Tuesday, so Urdu, which cannot be on Wednesday, is on Monday. Maths cannot be on Wednesday, because Physics would then have no later day, so Maths is also on Monday. English and Physics fill Wednesday, so Physics on Tuesday is impossible. Maths and Urdu share Monday in either order, so Maths in the morning is not forced, and Biology may be in either session.

questions.s: If Urdu is held in a morning session, which one of the following must be true?
o: Maths is held in an evening session
questions.e: Urdu is in a morning session, so its partner on the same day is in the evening. Chemistry and Biology are partners of each other, and English must be a morning paper, so Urdu's partner is Maths or Physics. If it is Maths, Maths is in the evening. If it is Physics, that day is Tuesday, Maths is on Monday and shares that day with English, who is in the morning, so Maths is again in the evening. The other options differ between valid timetables.

questions.s: If English is held on Tuesday, how many different timetables are possible?
questions.e: English is in the Tuesday morning, so its evening partner is Maths, Physics, Urdu, Chemistry or Biology. Chemistry or Biology would split that pair. Maths would force Physics onto Wednesday with a partner who cannot exist, since Urdu is barred from Wednesday and Chemistry and Biology must be together. Urdu would leave Maths on Monday with Chemistry or Biology, again splitting the pair. So Tuesday is English and Physics, Maths and Urdu share Monday in either order, and Chemistry and Biology share Wednesday in either order, giving 2 × 2 = 4 timetables.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the postings?
o: Lahore: Ahsan, Ehtisham; Multan: Beenish, Chand; Sialkot: Dania
Lahore: Ahsan, Chand, Dania; Multan: Beenish; Sialkot: Ehtisham
Lahore: Ahsan, Dania, Ehtisham; Multan: Beenish; Sialkot: Chand
Lahore: Beenish, Dania; Multan: Ahsan; Sialkot: Chand, Ehtisham
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Lahore: Beenish, Dania; Multan: Ahsan; Sialkot: Chand, Ehtisham satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Chand is posted to Lahore; Dania is in Multan or Sialkot but not with Ehtisham; Beenish and Chand are in different cities while Ehtisham is not in Sialkot.

questions.s: If Ehtisham is posted to Lahore, which one of the following must be true?
o: Beenish and Chand are posted to the same city
questions.e: Ehtisham is not in Sialkot, so the last rule applies and Beenish and Chand must be in the same city. Dania then has to be in Lahore, as she is with Ehtisham there. The other options are not forced: Ahsan may be in Multan or Sialkot, and Chand may be in either of those cities as well.

questions.s: If Ahsan is posted to Sialkot, which one of the following could be true?
o: Chand and Dania are posted to the same city
Beenish and Ehtisham are posted to the same city
questions.e: Ahsan and Ehtisham in Sialkot, Beenish and Chand in Multan and Dania in Lahore is valid, so Beenish can be in Multan. With Ahsan in Sialkot, Ehtisham in Multan would not be in Sialkot, so Beenish and Chand would have to share a city. They cannot be in Lahore or Sialkot, so they would be in Multan, making three there. The same pressure stops Dania, Chand and Ehtisham, or Beenish and Ehtisham, from sharing a city.

questions.s: If Dania is posted to Multan, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Dania is not in Lahore, so she must be with Ehtisham in Multan, which is then full. Ehtisham is not in Sialkot, so Beenish and Chand share a city. They cannot be in Multan, and Chand cannot be in Lahore, so both are in Sialkot. Lahore needs someone, and only Ahsan is left, so Ahsan is in Lahore.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
o: Three representatives are posted to Lahore
Ahsan and Chand are posted to the same city
Three representatives are posted to Sialkot
questions.e: If three were in Lahore, Multan and Sialkot would hold one each, and Chand would be alone in one of them. Beenish could not share his city, so the last rule needs Ehtisham in Sialkot, which puts Chand in Multan. Lahore then holds Ahsan, Beenish and Dania, which puts Ahsan and Beenish together. The other three options occur: Ahsan in Lahore, Beenish in Multan and the other three in Sialkot; Beenish in Lahore with Ahsan and Chand in Multan, Dania in Lahore, Ehtisham in Sialkot.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the three office-bearers?
o: Chairperson Gulnaz, Secretary Irfan, Treasurer Hassan
Chairperson Irfan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Javeria
Chairperson Irfan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Hassan
Chairperson Hassan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Irfan
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Chairperson Irfan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Hassan satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Gulnaz is Chairperson; Hassan holds a post other than Treasurer; Irfan and Javeria both hold posts.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
o: Irfan is Chairperson and Javeria is Secretary
Kamran is Chairperson and Javeria is Secretary
Irfan is Chairperson and Gulnaz is Secretary
Javeria is Chairperson and Hassan is Treasurer
questions.e: Irfan and Javeria are not both given posts, so they cannot hold two of the three posts together. Irfan as Chairperson with Gulnaz as Secretary, Kamran as Chairperson with Javeria as Secretary, and Javeria as Chairperson with Hassan as Treasurer are all possible: Irfan, Gulnaz, Hassan; Kamran, Javeria, Gulnaz; Javeria, Gulnaz, Hassan.

questions.s: If Kamran holds no post, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Without Kamran, the posts go to three of Gulnaz, Hassan, Irfan and Javeria. Irfan and Javeria cannot both serve, so Gulnaz and Hassan both serve, with Irfan or Javeria. Hassan must be Treasurer, and Gulnaz cannot be Chairperson, so Gulnaz is Secretary. Irfan or Javeria is Chairperson, so neither of those is forced, and Hassan cannot be Secretary.

questions.s: If Hassan holds a post, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Hassan, if he holds a post, is Treasurer, so Chairperson and Secretary come from Gulnaz, Irfan, Javeria and Kamran. Irfan as Secretary works with Kamran as Chairperson: Kamran, Irfan, Hassan. Gulnaz cannot be Chairperson, Kamran cannot be Treasurer and Hassan cannot be Secretary.

questions.s: If both Gulnaz and Kamran hold posts, in how many different ways can the three posts be filled?
questions.e: Gulnaz and Kamran hold two posts, and the third goes to Hassan, Irfan or Javeria. With Hassan, he must be Treasurer, so Kamran is Chairperson and Gulnaz Secretary: 1 way. With Irfan or Javeria (call the person X), Gulnaz cannot be Chairperson and Kamran cannot be Treasurer. Of the 6 ways to place the three people, 2 have Gulnaz as Chairperson and 2 have Kamran as Treasurer, and 1 has both, leaving 6 − 2 − 2 + 1 = 3 ways for each of X. That gives 1 + 2 × 3 = 7 ways.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the seating plan, listed from seat 1 to seat 6?
o: front row Adeel, Danyal, Eman; back row Fahad, Bushra, Ghazala
front row Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala; back row Bushra, Eman, Fahad
front row Adeel, Ghazala, Danyal; back row Eman, Fahad, Bushra
front row Adeel, Bushra, Danyal; back row Eman, Fahad, Ghazala
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. front row Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala; back row Bushra, Eman, Fahad satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Danyal is not directly in front of Bushra; Eman and Fahad are not in neighbouring seats of one row; Ghazala is in the middle column.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
o: Adeel sits in the front row
Ghazala sits in the front row
Eman sits in the front row
Adeel sits in the middle column
questions.e: If Danyal and Bushra shared the middle column, Eman and Fahad would have no two neighbouring free seats in either row, so Danyal and Bushra are in an end column. Each row then has two free seats, the middle one and the other end. Eman and Fahad fill both free seats of one row. Ghazala cannot take a middle seat, so she takes the end seat of the other row and Adeel its middle seat. Adeel is in the middle column. The other options fail in some valid plans: in Danyal, Eman, Fahad over Bushra, Adeel, Ghazala, Adeel and Ghazala sit at the back, and in Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala over Bushra, Eman, Fahad, Eman sits at the back.

questions.s: If Eman sits in the front row, which one of the following must be true?
o: Bushra and Ghazala sit in the same row
Eman sits in the middle column
questions.e: Eman is in the front row, so Fahad is too, and with Danyal that fills the front row. The back row then holds Bushra, Adeel and Ghazala. Danyal could be in seat 1 or seat 3, Ghazala in seat 4 or seat 6, and Eman in the middle or at an end, so those options are not forced.

questions.s: If Ghazala sits in seat 1, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Ghazala in seat 1 means Adeel is in the middle seat of the front row and Danyal in seat 3, so Bushra is in seat 6. Eman and Fahad share seats 4 and 5, so Eman can be in seat 4. Fahad cannot be in seat 6, Adeel cannot be in seat 5 and Bushra cannot be in seat 4.

questions.s: If Adeel sits in the front row, which one of the following cannot be true?
o: Eman sits in the front row
questions.e: Only four plans put Adeel in the front row: Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala over Bushra, Eman, Fahad; the same with Eman and Fahad swapped; Ghazala, Adeel, Danyal over Eman, Fahad, Bushra; and the same with Eman and Fahad swapped. Eman is in the back row every time. Bushra in seat 4, Ghazala in seat 3 and Fahad in seat 5 each appear.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the businesses on floors 1 to 5, in that order?
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Bank, Pharmacy, Clinic, Tailor, Lawyer satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: the Pharmacy is below the Bank; the Tailor is on floor 1 or floor 5; the Lawyer is below the Bank.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
o: The Tailor is above the Lawyer
The Pharmacy is on floor 4 or floor 5
The Bank is on floor 1 or floor 2
The Clinic is above the Bank
questions.e: The Bank is below the Pharmacy and the Lawyer, so only the Clinic and the Tailor could be below it. The Tailor is not on floor 1, so floor 1 is the Bank or the Clinic. If the Bank were above floor 2, both the Clinic and the Tailor would be below it, on floors 1 and 2. The Lawyer would then be on floor 4 or 5, three or four floors from the Clinic, not two. So the Bank is on floor 1 or 2. The other options fail in some valid arrangements, such as Clinic, Bank, Lawyer, Tailor, Pharmacy.

questions.s: If the Clinic is on floor 4, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: With the Clinic on floor 4, the Lawyer must be on floor 2 (floor 6 does not exist). The Bank is below the Pharmacy and the Lawyer, so the Bank is on floor 1. The Tailor cannot be on floor 5, so the Pharmacy is on floor 5 and the Tailor on floor 3.

questions.s: If the Tailor is on a higher floor than the Pharmacy, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: The Bank is below the Pharmacy and the Lawyer, and so below the Tailor too, so at most the Clinic can be lower: the Bank is on floor 1 or 2. If it were on floor 2, the Clinic would be on floor 1 and the Lawyer on floor 3, so the Tailor, who cannot be on floor 5, would be on floor 4 below the Pharmacy on floor 5, which breaks the condition. So the Bank is on floor 1. If the Clinic and the Lawyer were on floors 2 and 4, the Pharmacy and Tailor would take floors 3 and 5, putting the Tailor on floor 5, which is not allowed. So the Clinic and the Lawyer are on floors 3 and 5, in some order, and the Pharmacy and Tailor on floors 2 and 4. The Clinic can be on floor 5, but not on floor 4, and the Lawyer cannot be on floor 2.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: The Lawyer must be above the Bank, so the Lawyer cannot be on floor 1. The others all occur: the Tailor on floor 4 in Bank, Pharmacy, Clinic, Tailor, Lawyer; the Clinic on floor 1 in Clinic, Bank, Lawyer, Tailor, Pharmacy; the Pharmacy on floor 5 in Bank, Lawyer, Tailor, Clinic, Pharmacy.

questions.s: If Sarmad is paired with Tehmina, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: With Sarmad and Tehmina paired, the other four are Rida, Umar, Warda and Yahya. Umar and Warda cannot be together, so the pairs are Rida with Umar and Warda with Yahya, or Rida with Warda and Umar with Yahya. questions.s: In how many different ways can the six students be paired?
questions.e: Rida's partner is Umar, Warda or Yahya. Room 3's afternoon goes to Pervez or Rameen, and the other, who must be in the opposite session, takes the morning of Room 2, leaving Laila in the afternoon of Room 2. Two orders for Moiz and Nimra and two for Pervez and Rameen give 2 × 2 = 4 schedules.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?

questions.e: The Dictionary and the Encyclopedia stand left of the Atlas, and so left of the Geography text beside it. If both stood to its right, the single book between them would have to be the Biography, which is at an end. The Folktales in position 1 works in Folktales, Dictionary, Cookbook, Encyclopedia, Geography, Atlas, Biography. The Biography cannot be first, and the Dictionary cannot be in position 3, which would put the Encyclopedia in 4 and the Cookbook and Folktales next to each other. The Atlas is in position 6, not 7.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: The Dictionary must be left of the Encyclopedia, so the Encyclopedia cannot be in position 1. questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?

The Quetta train is at platform 5
The Sukkur train is at platform 3
The Multan train is at platform 2 or 3
questions.e: The Multan train cannot be at platform 1 or 5 (the Quetta train must be higher). If it were at platform 4, the Quetta train would be at 5, the Peshawar train at 1, and the Sukkur and Rawalpindi trains would be at the neighbouring platforms 2 and 3, which is not allowed. So the Multan train is at platform 2 or 3. “The Quetta train is at platform 5” is false in the valid arrangement (Rawalpindi, Multan, Quetta, Sukkur, Peshawar); “The Peshawar train is at platform 1” is false in the valid arrangement (Rawalpindi, Multan, Quetta, Sukkur, Peshawar); “The Sukkur train is at platform 3” is false in the valid arrangement (Rawalpindi, Multan, Quetta, Sukkur, Peshawar).

questions.s: If the Peshawar train is at platform 5, which one of the following must be true?

The Multan train is at platform 2
The Sukkur train is at platform 4
The Quetta train is at platform 3
questions.e: With the Peshawar train at platform 5, the Sukkur and Rawalpindi trains must be at platforms 1 and 3, 1 and 4, or 2 and 4. With 2 and 4 the Multan and Quetta trains would be at 1 and 3, which puts the Multan train at platform 1, and that is not allowed. In the other two cases the Multan and Quetta trains take platforms 2 and 4, or 2 and 3, so the Multan train is at platform 2. “The Quetta train is at platform 3” is false in the valid arrangement (Rawalpindi, Multan, Sukkur, Quetta, Peshawar); “The Rawalpindi train is at platform 1” is false in the valid arrangement (Sukkur, Multan, Quetta, Rawalpindi, Peshawar); “The Sukkur train is at platform 4” is false in the valid arrangement (Sukkur, Multan, Quetta, Rawalpindi, Peshawar).

questions.s: If the Quetta train is at platform 5, which one of the following could be true?
o: The Multan train is at platform 2
The Peshawar train is at platform 5
The Rawalpindi train is at platform 2
The Sukkur train is at platform 3
questions.e: With the Quetta train at platform 5, the Peshawar train is at platform 1, so the Multan, Rawalpindi and Sukkur trains share platforms 2 to 4. The Rawalpindi and Sukkur trains cannot be neighbours, so they are at platforms 2 and 4 and the Multan train is at platform 3. The Rawalpindi train can be at platform 2, as in Peshawar, Rawalpindi, Multan, Sukkur, Quetta. The Multan train cannot be at platform 2, the Sukkur train cannot be at platform 3 and the Peshawar train cannot be at platform 5.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
o: The Multan train is at platform 3
The Peshawar train is at platform 1

questions.e: The Quetta train must be at a higher platform than the Multan train, which is not at platform 1, so the Quetta train cannot be at platform 2 (that would need the Multan train at platform 1). The other options occur: “The Multan train is at platform 3” occurs in the valid arrangement (Peshawar, Rawalpindi, Multan, Quetta, Sukkur); “The Sukkur train is at platform 2” occurs in the valid arrangement (Peshawar, Sukkur, Multan, Quetta, Rawalpindi); “The Peshawar train is at platform 1” occurs in the valid arrangement (Peshawar, Multan, Rawalpindi, Quetta, Sukkur).

Dr Qadir is on duty on Wednesday
Dr Shams is on duty on Friday
Dr Rubina is on duty on Thursday
questions.e: Dr Rubina is on duty on Saturday and one earlier day. If she were also on duty on Tuesday, Dr Qadir would have to take Wednesday (Dr Shams may not, and Dr Rubina cannot follow herself), leaving Dr Shams to cover Thursday and Friday together, which is not allowed. So Tuesday is not Dr Rubina's, and it is not Dr Qadir's, so Dr Shams is on duty on Tuesday. “Dr Qadir is on duty on Wednesday” is false in the valid arrangement (Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina, Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina); “Dr Rubina is on duty on Thursday” is false in the valid arrangement (Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina, Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina); “Dr Shams is on duty on Friday” is false in the valid arrangement (Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina, Dr Shams, Dr Qadir, Dr Rubina).

questions.s: If Dr Qadir is on duty on Friday, which one of the following must be true?

Dr Shams is on duty on Thursday
Dr Qadir is on duty on Wednesday
questions.e: Dr Qadir works Monday and Friday. Wednesday cannot be Dr Qadir's (both days used) or Dr Shams's, so it is Dr Rubina's. Tuesday cannot then be Dr Rubina's, so it is Dr Shams's, and Thursday cannot be Dr Rubina's, so it is Dr Shams's, leaving Saturday for Dr Rubina. Dr Shams is on duty on Thursday.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
o: Dr Qadir is on duty on both Monday and Thursday
Dr Rubina is on duty on both Tuesday and Saturday
Dr Shams is on duty on both Thursday and Saturday
Dr Rubina is on duty on both Tuesday and Friday
questions.e: Dr Rubina on Tuesday and Saturday would force Dr Qadir onto Wednesday, since Dr Shams cannot work that day and Dr Rubina cannot follow herself. That leaves Dr Shams for both Thursday and Friday, which is not allowed. The other options occur: “Dr Rubina is on duty on both Tuesday and Friday” occurs in the valid arrangement (Dr Qadir, Dr Rubina, Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina, Dr Shams); “Dr Shams is on duty on both Thursday and Saturday” occurs in the valid arrangement (Dr Qadir, Dr Rubina, Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina, Dr Shams); “Dr Qadir is on duty on both Monday and Thursday” occurs in the valid arrangement (Dr Qadir, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina, Dr Qadir, Dr Rubina, Dr Shams).

questions.s: If Dr Shams is on duty on Tuesday, how many different rotas are possible?
questions.e: Dr Qadir is on Monday and Dr Shams on Tuesday. If Dr Qadir takes Wednesday too, Thursday to Saturday must be Dr Rubina, Dr Shams, Dr Rubina: 1 rota. If Dr Rubina takes Wednesday, the remaining days Thursday to Saturday hold one Qadir, one Rubina and one Shams, with Thursday not Dr Rubina's: Thursday Qadir leaves 2 orders for Friday and Saturday, and Thursday Shams leaves 2 orders. That is 4, so the total is 1 + 4 = 5.

questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Ali, Chaman, Dilshad, Behroz, Faraz, Gulrez, Eshaal satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Dilshad is ahead of Chaman; Eshaal is neither first nor last; Faraz and Gulrez are not next to each other.

questions.s: If Behroz is in position 4, which one of the following must be true?
o: Chaman and Dilshad stand next to each other
questions.e: Behroz is in position 4, so Ali is in position 1 or 7, and as he must be ahead of Chaman he is in position 1

questions.s: If Eshaal is in position 1, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Eshaal is first, so Ali cannot be first and must be ahead of Chaman and Dilshad. Chaman is therefore no earlier than position 3 and Dilshad no earlier than position 4, and Ali cannot be as far back as position 6. Dilshad in position 7 works in Eshaal, Ali, Faraz, Gulrez, Behroz, Chaman, Dilshad.

questions.s: If Gulrez is first in the queue, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Gulrez is first, so Faraz is second. Eshaal is then last, and positions 3 to 6 hold Ali, Chaman, Dilshad and Behroz. Ali is ahead of Chaman and Dilshad and three places from Behroz, so Ali is in position 3, Behroz in position 6, and Chaman and Dilshad in 4 and 5. “Chaman is in position 3” is false in the valid arrangement (Gulrez, Faraz, Ali, Chaman, Dilshad, Behroz, Eshaal); “Ali is in position 2” is false in the valid arrangement (Gulrez, Faraz, Ali, Chaman, Dilshad, Behroz, Eshaal); “Dilshad is in position 4” is false in the valid arrangement (Gulrez, Faraz, Ali, Chaman, Dilshad, Behroz, Eshaal).

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Behroz in position 3 would put Ali in position 6 (position 0 does not exist), but Ali must have Chaman and Dilshad behind him, so he cannot be in position 6. The other options occur: “Ali is in position 5” occurs in the valid arrangement (Eshaal, Behroz, Faraz, Gulrez, Ali, Chaman, Dilshad); “Dilshad is in position 7” occurs in the valid arrangement (Eshaal, Ali, Faraz, Gulrez, Behroz, Chaman, Dilshad); “Chaman is in position 6” occurs in the valid arrangement (Eshaal, Ali, Faraz, Gulrez, Behroz, Chaman, Dilshad).

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the delegation?
o: Mr Chishti, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Gulshan
Mr Aslam, Mr Chishti, Eman, Furqan
Mr Aslam, Ms Bilqis, Eman, Gulshan
Ms Bilqis, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Hamna
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Ms Bilqis, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Hamna satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Mr Aslam and Ms Bilqis are both selected; Mr Chishti is selected without Eman; Furqan is selected without Ms Durrani.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
o: Mr Chishti or Ms Durrani is selected
questions.e: Exactly two teachers are chosen and Mr Aslam and Ms Bilqis are not both chosen, so at least one teacher comes from Mr Chishti and Ms Durrani. Mr Aslam, Eman and Hamna are each absent from some valid delegation: “Mr Aslam is selected” is false in the valid arrangement (Ms Bilqis, Mr Chishti, Eman, Gulshan); “Eman is selected” is false in the valid arrangement (Mr Aslam, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Gulshan); “Hamna is selected” is false in the valid arrangement (Mr Aslam, Mr Chishti, Eman, Gulshan).

questions.s: If Eman is not selected, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Without Eman, Mr Chishti cannot be selected, so the two students come from Furqan, Gulshan and Hamna. Gulshan and Hamna are never both selected, so Furqan is selected, and Furqan needs Ms Durrani. “Mr Aslam is selected” is false in the valid arrangement (Ms Bilqis, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Gulshan); “Gulshan is selected” is false in the valid arrangement (Mr Aslam, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Hamna); “Hamna is not selected” is false in the valid arrangement (Mr Aslam, Ms Durrani, Furqan, Hamna).

questions.s: If Mr Aslam is selected, which one of the following could be true?
o: Gulshan and Hamna are both selected
Mr Chishti and Ms Durrani are both selected
questions.e: With Mr Aslam selected, Ms Bilqis is not, and the second teacher is Mr Chishti or Ms Durrani, so they are not both selected. Furqan can be selected when Ms Durrani is the second teacher, as in Mr Aslam, Ms Durrani, Eman, Furqan.

questions.s: If Ms Durrani is not selected, how many different delegations are possible?
questions.e: Without Ms Durrani, the teachers are Mr Chishti and one of Mr Aslam and Ms Bilqis (not both): 2 choices. Furqan is out, since he needs Ms Durrani, and Mr Chishti needs Eman, so the students are Eman with Gulshan or Eman with Hamna: 2 choices. The total is 2 × 2 = 4.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the order of speakers, first to last?
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Dua, Aamir, Benish, Ehsan, Chand satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Aamir speaks before Benish and Chand is not last; Dua and Ehsan speak in consecutive places and Dua is not first; Chand speaks before Ehsan.

questions.s: If Aamir speaks first, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Aamir speaks first, so he is before Benish and Chand must speak last. Dua and Ehsan cannot be in consecutive places (Dua is not first), so they take positions 2 and 4, which leaves position 3 for Benish. “Dua speaks second” is false in the valid arrangement (Aamir, Ehsan, Benish, Dua, Chand); “Ehsan speaks fourth” is false in the valid arrangement (Aamir, Ehsan, Benish, Dua, Chand); “Chand speaks fourth” is false in the valid arrangement (Aamir, Dua, Benish, Ehsan, Chand).

questions.s: If Benish speaks before Aamir, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Benish before Aamir leaves Chand free to speak earlier than last. Chand can speak second, as in Ehsan, Chand, Benish, Aamir, Dua. Ehsan cannot speak last, since he must be before Chand. Benish cannot speak first. Dua cannot speak immediately after Ehsan, because they would be consecutive with Dua not first.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Ehsan must speak before Chand, so Chand cannot speak first. The others are possible: “Aamir speaks last” occurs in the valid arrangement (Ehsan, Benish, Chand, Dua, Aamir); “Dua speaks second” occurs in the valid arrangement (Aamir, Dua, Benish, Ehsan, Chand); “Benish speaks fourth” occurs in the valid arrangement (Dua, Aamir, Ehsan, Benish, Chand).

questions.s: If Chand speaks fourth, how many different orders are possible?
questions.e: Chand is fourth, so not last, and the first rule then needs Benish before Aamir. Ehsan is before Chand. The last speaker is Aamir or Dua (Benish must be before Aamir, and Ehsan before Chand). If Dua is last, Benish cannot be first, so Ehsan is first, Benish second and Aamir third: 1 order. If Aamir is last, Benish, Dua and Ehsan fill the first three places with Benish not first and Dua and Ehsan not consecutive unless Dua is first: Dua, Benish, Ehsan; Dua, Ehsan, Benish; Ehsan, Benish, Dua: 3 orders. The total is 4.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the seating, from chair 1 to chair 8?
o: Zeenat, Yawar, Uzair, Tania, Xari, Waqas, Raza, Sadaf
Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Tania, Yawar, Sadaf, Uzair, Raza
Zeenat, Xari, Uzair, Tania, Yawar, Waqas, Raza, Sadaf
Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Tania, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Sadaf
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Tania, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Sadaf satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Yawar is not opposite Zeenat; Xari and Waqas are not neighbours; Tania is not opposite Sadaf.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Zeenat is in chair 1 and Yawar in chair 5. Uzair has exactly one chair between him and Zeenat, so he is in chair 3 or 7. Tania and Sadaf are opposite, so they use chairs 2 and 6 or 4 and 8, since Uzair occupies one of 3 and 7. The other even pair and the remaining odd chair are left for Xari, Waqas and Raza. Xari and Waqas must be neighbours, so they take the odd chair and its even neighbour, and Raza takes the other even chair, which is next to Uzair. “Raza sits next to Zeenat” is false in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Tania, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Sadaf); “Xari sits next to Zeenat” is false in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Waqas, Xari, Tania, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Sadaf); “Tania sits next to Yawar” is false in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Sadaf, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Tania).

questions.s: If Uzair sits in chair 3, which one of the following must be true?
o: Exactly one chair separates Raza and Tania
questions.e: Uzair is in chair 3, so Tania and Sadaf cannot use chairs 3 and 7 and take chairs 2 and 6 or chairs 4 and 8. In the first case chairs 4, 7 and 8 remain for Xari, Waqas and Raza, and Xari and Waqas must be neighbours, so they take 7 and 8 and Raza takes chair 4. In the second case chairs 2, 6 and 7 remain, Xari and Waqas take 6 and 7, and Raza takes chair 2. Either way exactly one chair separates Raza from Tania. “Waqas sits in chair 6” is false in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Raza, Uzair, Tania, Yawar, Xari, Waqas, Sadaf); “Raza sits in chair 4” is false in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Raza, Uzair, Tania, Yawar, Xari, Waqas, Sadaf); “Xari sits next to Yawar” is false in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Raza, Uzair, Tania, Yawar, Waqas, Xari, Sadaf).

questions.s: If Raza sits in chair 2, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: With Raza in chair 2, Tania and Sadaf cannot use chairs 2 and 6, and Uzair takes one of chairs 3 and 7, so they cannot use 3 and 7 either; they take chairs 4 and 8. If Uzair were in chair 7, Xari and Waqas would be left with chairs 3 and 6, which are not neighbours, so Uzair is in chair 3 and Xari and Waqas take 6 and 7. Tania can be in chair 4, as in Zeenat, Raza, Uzair, Tania, Yawar, Xari, Waqas, Sadaf. Xari cannot be in chair 8, Uzair cannot be in chair 7 and Tania cannot be in chair 6.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Uzair must have exactly one chair between him and Zeenat, so he is in chair 3 or 7, never chair 4. The others occur: “Raza sits in chair 6” occurs in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Tania, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Sadaf); “Xari sits in chair 2” occurs in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Tania, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Sadaf); “Tania sits in chair 8” occurs in the valid arrangement (Zeenat, Xari, Waqas, Sadaf, Yawar, Raza, Uzair, Tania).

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the way the parcels are shared?
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Naeem: 3, 5; Obaid: 1, 2, 4; Pari: 6 satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: parcels 1 and 2 go to different couriers; parcels 3 and 4 go to the same courier; parcel 5 does not go to Naeem.

questions.s: If parcel 6 goes to Naeem, which one of the following must be true?
o: Parcel 1 does not go to Naeem
questions.e: Naeem has parcels 5 and 6, and parcel 6 cannot go with parcel 1, so parcel 1 does not go to Naeem. “Parcel 3 goes to Naeem” is false in the valid arrangement (Naeem: 5, 6; Obaid: 1, 2, 3; Pari: 4); “Parcel 4 goes to Obaid” is false in the valid arrangement (Naeem: 5, 6; Obaid: 1, 2, 3; Pari: 4); “Parcel 1 goes to Pari” is false in the valid arrangement (Naeem: 5, 6; Obaid: 1, 2, 3; Pari: 4).

questions.s: If parcel 3 goes to Naeem, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Parcel 3 goes to Naeem, so parcel 4 goes to Obaid or Pari. If parcel 4 went to Pari, parcel 3 would have to go to Obaid, which it does not, so parcel 4 goes to Obaid. “Parcel 6 goes to Naeem” is false in the valid arrangement (Naeem: 3, 5; Obaid: 1, 2, 4; Pari: 6); “Parcel 1 goes to Obaid” is false in the valid arrangement (Naeem: 3, 5, 6; Obaid: 4; Pari: 1, 2); “Parcel 2 goes to Pari” is false in the valid arrangement (Naeem: 3, 5; Obaid: 1, 2, 4; Pari: 6).

questions.s: If parcel 1 goes to Pari, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Pari has parcels 1 and 2, so parcel 6 cannot go to Pari and parcel 2 cannot go to Naeem. If Obaid had three parcels, Naeem and Pari would have one and two, and Pari already has parcels 1 and 2, so Naeem would have only parcel 5 and Obaid parcels 3, 4 and 6, which puts 3 and 4 together, which is not allowed. Parcel 6 can go to Obaid, as in Naeem: 3, 5; Obaid: 4, 6; Pari: 1, 2.

questions.s: If Naeem delivers parcels 5 and 6, how many different ways can the parcels be shared?
questions.e: Naeem has parcels 5 and 6, so parcels 1 and 2 go together to Obaid or Pari. If they go to Obaid, parcels 3 and 4 must put Pari on the list: parcel 3 to Obaid and parcel 4 to Pari, parcel 3 to Pari and parcel 4 to Obaid, or parcel 3 to Pari and parcel 4 to Naeem, which makes 3 distributions. If they go to Pari, parcels 3 and 4 must put Obaid on the list: parcel 3 to Obaid and parcel 4 to Naeem, parcel 3 to Obaid and parcel 4 to Pari, parcel 3 to Naeem and parcel 4 to Obaid, or parcel 3 to Pari and parcel 4 to Obaid, which makes 4. The total is 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the seating, from place 1 to place 6?
o: Fahim, Alina, Bashir, Esha, Danial, Cyma
Esha, Danial, Cyma, Bashir, Alina, Fahim
Alina, Bashir, Danial, Esha, Fahim, Cyma
Alina, Danial, Cyma, Bashir, Esha, Fahim
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Fahim, Alina, Bashir, Esha, Danial, Cyma satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Bashir sits to the left of Alina; Danial and Esha are not neighbours; Fahim is not at an end.

questions.s: If Fahim sits in place 1, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Fahim is in place 1, so the three women, who cannot be neighbours, must take places 2, 4 and 6. Cyma is right of Danial, so she is not in place 2. If she were in place 4, Danial would be in place 3, left of her, Esha would be beside him in place 2, and Alina would be in place 6 with no place for Bashir on her right. So Cyma is in place 6. “Alina sits in place 2” is false in the valid arrangement (Fahim, Esha, Danial, Alina, Bashir, Cyma); “Danial sits in place 3” is false in the valid arrangement (Fahim, Alina, Bashir, Esha, Danial, Cyma); “Esha sits in place 4” is false in the valid arrangement (Fahim, Esha, Danial, Alina, Bashir, Cyma).

questions.s: If Alina sits in place 1, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Alina in place 1 and Fahim at an end means Fahim is in place 6, and the women must then take places 1, 3 and 5. Esha cannot be in place 5, because Danial would then be in place 4 with Cyma on his left, so Esha is in place 3 and Cyma in place 5, and Danial and Bashir take places 2 and 4 in either order. Danial can be in place 2, as in Alina, Danial, Esha, Bashir, Cyma, Fahim. Bashir is never in place 3, Cyma never in place 4 and Esha never in place 5.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: Suppose Cyma sat in place 4. Alina and Esha could not take places 3 or 5, so they would take two of places 1, 2 and 6, and, not being neighbours, places 1 and 6. Alina cannot be in place 6, since Bashir must be on her right, so Esha is in place 6 and Danial in place 5, which is right of Cyma. So Cyma cannot be in place 4. The others occur: “Alina sits in place 4” occurs in the valid arrangement (Fahim, Esha, Danial, Alina, Bashir, Cyma); “Bashir sits in place 5” occurs in the valid arrangement (Fahim, Alina, Danial, Esha, Bashir, Cyma); “Fahim sits in place 6” occurs in the valid arrangement (Alina, Bashir, Esha, Danial, Cyma, Fahim).

questions.s: If Fahim sits in place 6, how many different seatings are possible?
questions.e: Fahim in place 6 puts the women in places 1, 3 and 5. Alina cannot be in place 5, as Bashir would have no place on her right, and Esha cannot be in place 5, because Danial would then be in place 4 with Cyma to his left. So Cyma is in place 5. If Esha is in place 1, Danial is in place 2, Alina in place 3 and Bashir in place 4. If Esha is in place 3, Alina is in place 1, and Danial and Bashir take places 2 and 4 in either order. That is 1 + 2 = 3 seatings.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the final table, from first place to sixth place?
o: Lions, Hawks, Tigers, Panthers, Eagles, Wolves
Tigers, Lions, Eagles, Hawks, Panthers, Wolves
Hawks, Lions, Tigers, Panthers, Eagles, Wolves
Lions, Hawks, Tigers, Wolves, Eagles, Panthers
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Lions, Hawks, Tigers, Panthers, Eagles, Wolves satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: the Hawks finish above the Lions; the Panthers finish first or last; the Tigers finish above the Lions.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
o: The Lions finish first or second
The Tigers finish below the Hawks
questions.e: The Lions finish above the Hawks, the Tigers and the Wolves (who are below the Hawks), so at least three teams are below them and they finish first, second or third. If they were third, the two teams above would be the Eagles and the Panthers, with the Panthers not first, so the Eagles would be first and the Panthers second, and the Tigers, two places from the Eagles, would be third, which the Lions occupy. So the Lions finish first or second. “The Lions finish first” is false in the valid arrangement (Eagles, Lions, Tigers, Hawks, Panthers, Wolves); “The Hawks finish second” is false in the valid arrangement (Lions, Tigers, Hawks, Eagles, Panthers, Wolves); “The Tigers finish below the Hawks” is false in the valid arrangement (Lions, Tigers, Hawks, Eagles, Panthers, Wolves).

questions.s: If the Panthers finish second, which one of the following must be true?
o: The Wolves finish fifth or sixth
questions.e: The Lions finish above the Hawks, the Tigers and the Wolves, so they are first or third once the Panthers hold second. Third would need the Eagles first, which puts the Tigers, two places away, in third as well, so the Lions are first. The Hawks, Tigers, Eagles and Wolves fill places 3 to 6, with the Wolves below the Hawks. The Wolves in place 4 would put the Hawks in place 3 and leave the Tigers and Eagles in places 5 and 6, which are neighbours, so the Wolves are fifth or sixth. “The Hawks finish third” is false in the valid arrangement (Lions, Panthers, Tigers, Hawks, Eagles, Wolves); “The Tigers finish third” is false in the valid arrangement (Lions, Panthers, Hawks, Tigers, Wolves, Eagles); “The Eagles finish sixth” is false in the valid arrangement (Lions, Panthers, Hawks, Eagles, Wolves, Tigers).

questions.s: If the Tigers finish third, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: With the Tigers third, the Eagles are first or fifth. Place 6 cannot go to the Lions or the Hawks (both must finish above other teams), the Panthers or the Tigers, so it goes to the Wolves, which rules out the Wolves in fifth. The Panthers can finish second, as in Lions, Panthers, Tigers, Hawks, Eagles, Wolves. The Eagles cannot finish second, which is next to third, and the Hawks cannot finish third, which the Tigers hold.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: The Lions finish above the Hawks, so the Hawks cannot finish first. The others are possible: “The Eagles finish first” occurs in the valid arrangement (Eagles, Lions, Tigers, Hawks, Panthers, Wolves); “The Lions finish second” occurs in the valid arrangement (Eagles, Lions, Tigers, Hawks, Panthers, Wolves); “The Wolves finish third” occurs in the valid arrangement (Lions, Hawks, Wolves, Tigers, Panthers, Eagles).

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the cousins in order of height, tallest first?
o: Rehan, Shazia, Taimur, Uzma, Wajid, Vaqar
Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Taimur, Wajid, Vaqar
Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Wajid, Taimur, Vaqar
Shazia, Rehan, Uzma, Wajid, Taimur, Vaqar
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Wajid, Taimur, Vaqar satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Shazia is taller than Rehan; Uzma and Wajid are not next to each other in height; Taimur is taller than Uzma.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Rehan is taller than Shazia and Shazia is taller than Vaqar, so Rehan is taller than Vaqar. “Shazia is taller than Uzma” is false in the valid arrangement (Rehan, Uzma, Wajid, Shazia, Taimur, Vaqar); “Taimur is taller than Shazia” is false in the valid arrangement (Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Wajid, Taimur, Vaqar); “Wajid is taller than Rehan” is false in the valid arrangement (Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Wajid, Taimur, Vaqar).

questions.s: If Shazia is the second tallest, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: Shazia is second, and Rehan is taller than her, so Rehan is tallest. “Vaqar is the shortest” is false in the valid arrangement (Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Wajid, Vaqar, Taimur); “Uzma is third tallest” is false in the valid arrangement (Rehan, Shazia, Wajid, Uzma, Taimur, Vaqar); “Taimur is fifth tallest” is false in the valid arrangement (Rehan, Shazia, Uzma, Wajid, Vaqar, Taimur).

questions.s: If Rehan is the third tallest, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: Two cousins are taller than Rehan, and they cannot be Shazia or Vaqar. Taimur is shorter than Uzma, so Taimur could be taller than Rehan only if Uzma were too, making Uzma and Taimur the two tallest and leaving Wajid no place next to Uzma. So Uzma and Wajid are the two tallest, and Shazia, Taimur and Vaqar fill places 4 to 6, with Shazia taller than Vaqar. Taimur can be fifth, as in Uzma, Wajid, Rehan, Shazia, Taimur, Vaqar. Shazia cannot be second, Vaqar cannot be fourth and Wajid cannot be fourth.

questions.s: If Uzma is the tallest, how many different orders are possible?
questions.e: Uzma is tallest, so Wajid, who is next to her in height, is second, and Taimur is shorter than both. Rehan, Shazia and Vaqar must stay in that order, and Taimur can take any of the four places 3 to 6 among them. That gives 4 orders.

questions.s: Which one of the following could be the programme, with each session's start time?
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Lecture 9:00; Workshop 10:00; Debate 12:00; Quiz 13:00; Demo 14:00 satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: the Workshop is held before the Lecture; the Quiz starts before 12:00; the Debate and the Demo are held one straight after the other.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: The Lecture comes before both the Workshop and the Quiz, so it cannot be later than third. If it were third, the first two sessions would be the Debate and the Demo, back to back, which is not allowed. So the Lecture is first, starting at 9:00, or second, starting at 10:00 after a one-hour session. “The Quiz starts at 13:00” is false in the valid arrangement (Lecture 9:00; Debate 10:00; Workshop 11:00; Demo 13:00; Quiz 14:00); “The Workshop starts at 11:00” is false in the valid arrangement (Lecture 9:00; Workshop 10:00; Debate 12:00; Quiz 13:00; Demo 14:00); “The Debate starts at 9:00” is false in the valid arrangement (Lecture 9:00; Workshop 10:00; Debate 12:00; Quiz 13:00; Demo 14:00).

questions.s: If the Quiz starts at 12:00, which one of the following must be true?
questions.e: The Quiz starts at 12:00, so three hours of sessions come before it. The Workshop and the Lecture would take three hours with nothing else, leaving the Debate and the Demo back to back after the Quiz, which is not allowed. So the Lecture, the Debate and the Demo come before the Quiz, with the Lecture between the other two, and the Workshop runs from 13:00 to 15:00. “The Lecture starts at 9:00” is false in the valid arrangement (Debate 9:00; Lecture 10:00; Demo 11:00; Quiz 12:00; Workshop 13:00); “The Debate starts at 9:00” is false in the valid arrangement (Demo 9:00; Lecture 10:00; Debate 11:00; Quiz 12:00; Workshop 13:00); “The Demo starts at 11:00” is false in the valid arrangement (Demo 9:00; Lecture 10:00; Debate 11:00; Quiz 12:00; Workshop 13:00).

questions.s: If the Debate starts at 9:00, which one of the following could be true?
questions.e: The Debate is first, so the second session cannot be the Demo (back to back with the Debate), the Workshop (the Lecture must come before it) or the Quiz (it cannot start at 10:00). So the Lecture is second, at 10:00. The Demo can be last, as in Debate 9:00; Lecture 10:00; Workshop 11:00; Quiz 13:00; Demo 14:00. The Workshop cannot start at 10:00, the Quiz cannot start at 11:00 and the Lecture cannot start at 11:00.

questions.s: Which one of the following cannot be true?
questions.e: The Quiz must start at 12:00 or later, so it cannot start at 11:00. The others are possible: “The Quiz starts at 14:00” occurs in the valid arrangement (Lecture 9:00; Debate 10:00; Workshop 11:00; Demo 13:00; Quiz 14:00); “The Workshop starts at 13:00” occurs in the valid arrangement (Debate 9:00; Lecture 10:00; Demo 11:00; Quiz 12:00; Workshop 13:00); “The Demo starts at 9:00” occurs in the valid arrangement (Demo 9:00; Lecture 10:00; Workshop 11:00; Quiz 13:00; Debate 14:00).

questions.s: Which one of the following could be each friend's subject and city?
o: Hasan Chemistry Quetta; Ifra Physics Karachi; Javed Mathematics Lahore; Kausar Computer Science Peshawar
Hasan Chemistry Karachi; Ifra Mathematics Peshawar; Javed Physics Lahore; Kausar Computer Science Quetta
Hasan Chemistry Karachi; Ifra Mathematics Quetta; Javed Computer Science Peshawar; Kausar Physics Lahore
Hasan Chemistry Karachi; Ifra Physics Lahore; Javed Mathematics Peshawar; Kausar Computer Science Quetta
questions.e: Test each option against the rules. Hasan Chemistry Karachi; Ifra Mathematics Peshawar; Javed Physics Lahore; Kausar Computer Science Quetta satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Ifra studies Mathematics and also lives in Karachi, or does neither; Kausar neither studies Computer Science nor lives in Peshawar; the Physics student lives outside Lahore.

questions.s: Which one of the following must be true?

questions.s: A study finds that cities with more cycle lanes have fewer road accidents, so the mayor plans more lanes to cut accidents. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
o: Cycle lanes cost much less to build than flyovers do.
Many people in the city already own and use bicycles.
Those cities also have lower speed limits and stricter enforcement.
The mayor has also promised to plant more trees.
questions.e: Other differences between the cities could explain the fewer accidents, so lanes may not be the cause. The other options are not about what causes accidents.

questions.s: The company's last two directors were from Lahore, and both resigned in the first year. The board decides that no one from Lahore can hold the post for long. The reasoning above is flawed because it
o: attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
treats a needed condition as if it were enough
draws a general claim from a very small group
questions.e: Two cases cannot support a claim about everyone from Lahore.

questions.s: Either we cancel the school trip, or we let students travel without teachers. We cannot let them travel without teachers, so we must cancel the trip. The reasoning above is flawed because it
o: attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
draws a general claim from a very small group
offers only two choices when more are possible
treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
questions.e: There are other options, such as sending teachers with them or changing the destination.

questions.s: A farmer will sow wheat two weeks earlier this year so that the crop is harvested before the monsoon rains. The farmer assumes that
o: other farmers will also sow two weeks earlier than usual.
the price of wheat will rise before the monsoon arrives.
the farmer will need extra labour at harvest time.
the rains will not arrive earlier than usual.
questions.e: If the rains came early, the earlier sowing would not beat them. Water needs, prices and other farmers do not matter to the plan.

questions.s: The town built a new bypass to reduce traffic in its centre, yet traffic in the centre increased. Which of the following, if true, best explains the apparent contradiction?
o: Easier access to the shops drew more people into the centre.
The bypass was built using concrete and strong steel.
The bypass has two lanes in each direction for traffic and a footpath.
Heavy goods vehicles are the main users of the bypass.
questions.e: If the bypass attracted more people to the centre, it could raise traffic there. The other options do not explain the rise.

questions.s: Farah says: 'The library's membership fell after it moved to a new building, so the move must have driven readers away.' Farah assumes that
o: the new building is harder to reach than the old one was.
most readers had been unhappy with the old building's facilities.
the library cut its opening hours after it moved.
membership would not have fallen anyway for some other reason.
questions.e: To blame the move, Farah must rule out other causes of the fall. 'Libraries lose members whenever they move' is a general rule she does not need, and distance is not mentioned.

questions.s: No one has ever proved that the old well is unsafe to drink from. So the well must be safe. The reasoning above is flawed because it
o: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
takes a lack of proof against a claim as proof that it is true
draws a general claim from a very small group
attacks the speaker instead of answering the claim made
questions.e: Nobody having proved it unsafe does not prove it safe; it may simply not have been tested.

questions.s: Statements: A firm has 40 employees. Of these, 25 can drive and 18 can speak English. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?
o: At least 18 employees are unable to drive a car.
Exactly 3 employees can both drive and speak English in this firm.
No employee in the firm can do both of these things.
At least 3 employees can both drive and speak English.
questions.e: 25 + 18 = 43, which exceeds 40, so at least 43 − 40 = 3 people are counted twice. 'Exactly 3' is not certain, since the overlap could be larger; and 40 − 25 = 15 cannot drive, not 18.

questions.s: Imran says: 'You must either support my plan fully or you are against the school.' The reasoning above is flawed because it
o: treats a link between two events as proof of a cause
draws a general claim from a very small group
uses its own conclusion as one of its reasons
offers only two choices when more are possible
questions.e: A person could support part of the plan, or disagree with it and still be loyal to the school.

questions.s: A government hospital added a second registration counter. A visitor concludes that patients now receive treatment sooner. Which assumption does the argument rely on?
o: The second counter was staffed by experienced clerks.
Most patients registered at the hospital are admitted as inpatients.
The hospital treats fewer patients now than it did last year.
Registration was a major part of the delay patients faced.
questions.e: If long registration queues were not the main delay, a second counter would not speed up treatment. Appointments and extra doctors are different causes that the visitor does not mention.

questions.s: The government says banning plastic bags will cut litter in the city. Which of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
o: Plastic bags are very cheap and widely used by shops.
Some shops already give customers paper bags instead.
The ban is due to take effect from the very start of January.
Most litter in the city is food wrappers and bottles, not bags.
questions.e: If bags make up little of the litter, banning them will not cut litter much.

questions.s: Bakeries in Gulberg open at 6 a.m. Fresh Bake is a bakery in Gulberg. Which conclusion is best supported by the statements?

Fresh Bake is the oldest bakery in Gulberg.
questions.e: Fresh Bake belongs to the group of Gulberg bakeries that open at 6 a.m. Price, closing time and age are not given.

questions.s: Statements: In Hira's class, everyone who takes drawing also takes music. Bilal does not take music. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?

Everyone who takes music takes drawing.
questions.e: If Bilal took drawing he would take music, but he does not. So he does not take drawing. The reverse does not follow.

questions.s: Statements: All the buses on Route 5 are air-conditioned. Some buses on Route 5 are old. Which of the following can be inferred from the statements?

questions.s: A town council says brighter paint on zebra crossings will cut pedestrian accidents. Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?
